heroHeadline: Trump Returns from Beijing, Offers 20-Year Iran Nuclear Suspension; House War Powers Vote Fails 212-212; Warsh Officially Fed Chair as Powell's Term Expires May 15; Approval at Second-Term Lows
heroSubtitle: President Trump returned to Washington May 15 (Day 476) after his two-day Beijing summit with Xi Jinping — the first US presidential China visit since his own 2017 trip — as China disputed Trump's claims of 'fantastic trade deals,' including a purported commitment by Beijing to buy 200 Boeing aircraft. On Air Force One, Trump signaled a potential Iran diplomatic off-ramp: he said he would accept Iran suspending nuclear enrichment for 20 years with a 'real commitment,' the most flexible US position to date in the 77-day-old US-Iran war. The House failed to advance an Iran war powers resolution on May 15 in a 212-212 tied vote — the third consecutive Democratic defeat on the issue. On the domestic front, Kevin Warsh officially became Federal Reserve Chair on May 16 when Jerome Powell's chairmanship expired May 15; Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Chair is June 16-17. Multiple May 2026 polls show Trump's approval at second-term lows: Silver Bulletin aggregate at ~36.8%/59.7% (net -18.9); Pew Research at 34%; only 25% among independents. Trump urged Louisiana Republicans to vote out Sen. Bill Cassidy in the May 16 primary, endorsing challenger Julia Letlow. The White House also released its 2026 US Counterterrorism Strategy, the first of Trump's second term.
